issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff with clear, document-supported title may sue for possession without seeking a declaration of title when the defendant has not raised a serious cloud over that title.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought possession on the strength of a registered sale deed from the person found to have inherited the property as the surviving heir.
The defendant claimed to have inherited the property as an adopted daughter, but the adoption was not proved in any court.
The parties litigated title and adoption, and the courts found no serious cloud on the plaintiff’s title.
issues.conclusion: The suit for possession was maintainable without a separate prayer for declaration of title.
issues.legal_principle: Under Anathula Sudhakar v. P. Buchi Reddy (2008) 4 SCC 594 and Kurella Naga Druva Yudaya Bhaskara Rao v. Galla Jani Kamma (2008) 15 SCC 150, a declaration is necessary only when denial of title or a third party’s apparent right raises a serious cloud over the plaintiff’s title; a suit for possession based on clear title is maintainable without it. The Court distinguished a summary suit under Section 6 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963.

rule.if: title_based_possession_suit and plaintiff_has_document_supported_title and not serious_cloud_over_title

predicates.title_based_possession_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit to recover possession on the basis of claimed title, rather than a summary suit based only on prior possession.
predicates.plaintiff_has_document_supported_title: The plaintiff relied on documents supporting the claimed title to the property.
predicates.serious_cloud_over_title: The defendant showed an apparent defect in the plaintiff’s title or a prima facie right of a third party over the property.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff brings a title-based possession suit, has document-supported title, and faces no serious cloud over that title, the suit may proceed without a declaration.

issues.legal_issue: A denial of a pleaded fact made only for want of knowledge does not specifically deny that fact, and an executant need not be examined to prove execution when execution has not been specifically disputed.
material_facts: The defendants’ written statement denied knowledge of the sale deed but did not specifically deny its execution.
The defendant who testified said she did not know whether the deed had been executed and did not deny that it had been.
The evidence supported execution of the deed.
issues.conclusion: Execution of the sale deed was not specifically disputed, so it was unnecessary to examine the executant to prove execution.
issues.legal_principle: Order 8 Rule 5 requires a specific answer to pleaded facts. Jahuri Sah v. Dwarika Prasad Jhunjhunwala, AIR 1967 SC 109, holds that lack of knowledge is not a denial, even an implied one. The Court also relied on Dhanbai v. State of M.P., 1978 MPLJ 717, and Samrathmal v. Union of India, AIR 1959 MP 305.

rule.if: civil_property_suit and sale_execution_pleaded and written_statement_only_claims_lack_of_knowledge and not specific_denial_of_execution

predicates.civil_property_suit: The parties litigated a civil claim concerning rights in property.
predicates.sale_execution_pleaded: A party pleaded that a sale document had been executed in its favour.
predicates.written_statement_only_claims_lack_of_kn: The opposing party answered that it lacked knowledge of the pleaded execution.
predicates.specific_denial_of_execution: The opposing party expressly disputed that the sale document had been executed.

issues.definition: In a civil property suit, when execution is pleaded but the response only claims lack of knowledge and does not specifically deny execution, the executant need not be examined to prove it.

issues.legal_issue: Material testimony ordinarily stands accepted when the opposing party does not challenge it in cross-examination.
material_facts: The plaintiff’s witnesses testified to the execution of the sale deed.
The defendants did not cross-examine those witnesses on the fact of execution.
issues.conclusion: The unchallenged evidence of execution should ordinarily have been accepted, and the High Court erred in finding that execution had not been proved.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that cross-examination is a matter of substance and that a party must put its version to the opposing witness. It relied on Bhoju Mandal v. Debnath Bhagat, AIR 1963 SC 1906; Chuni Lal Dwarka Nath v. Hartford Fire Insurance Co., AIR 1958 Punjab 440; Maroti Bansi Teli v. Radhabai, AIR 1945 Nagpur 60; A.E.G. Carapiet v. A.Y. Derderian, AIR 1961 Cal. 359; Kuwarlal Amritlal v. Rekhlal Koduram, AIR 1950 Nagpur 83; and Karnidan Sarda v. Sailaja Kanta Mitra, AIR 1940 Patna 683.

predicates.civil_case: The testimony was given in a civil proceeding.
predicates.witness_gives_material_testimony: A witness gives testimony about a fact material to deciding the dispute.
predicates.opposing_party_cross_examines_on_that_te: The opposing party questions the witness in cross-examination about that material testimony.

issues.definition: In a civil case, material testimony that the opposing party does not test in cross-examination is ordinarily accepted.

issues.legal_issue: A third party who has not established a legal interest in a sale cannot challenge whether consideration passed under the sale deed.
material_facts: The defendant challenged the sale deed on the ground that consideration had not passed.
The defendant’s asserted status as an adopted daughter and heir was not proved.
The defendant was therefore a third party to the sale deed.
issues.conclusion: The defendant could not challenge the passing of consideration under the sale deed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle that a third party cannot question the passing of consideration under a sale deed, relying on Pandit Ramjilal Tiwari v. Vijai Kumar, 1970 MPLJ 50, and noting the consistent views in Mt. Akli v. Mt. Daho, AIR 1928 Patna 44, and Maroti Bansi Teli v. Radhabai, AIR 1945 Nagpur 60.

predicates.sale_deed_consideration_challenged: A person disputes whether consideration passed under a sale deed.
predicates.challenger_is_not_party_or_representativ: The person challenging consideration was neither a party to the sale nor a representative of a party.
predicates.challenger_has_not_established_legal_int: The challenger did not establish an independent legal interest in the property that would entitle them to contest the sale.

issues.definition: A person who is neither a party nor a representative and has not established a legal interest cannot challenge whether consideration passed under a sale deed.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser with title under a valid sale deed may recover possession even if the seller did not deliver possession at the time of sale.
material_facts: The person who executed the sale deed had inherited the property and had the right to sell it.
The plaintiff’s title under the sale deed was established.
The seller may not have delivered possession to the plaintiff when the deed was executed.
The defendant’s adoption claim was not proved, and revenue entries showing possession did not establish a right to retain the property.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff was entitled to recover possession on the strength of title despite the possible absence of delivery of possession by the seller.
issues.legal_principle: A plaintiff who establishes title may recover possession on that title; prior delivery of possession by the seller is not necessary to that entitlement. A revenue entry recording possession, without more, does not confer a right to retain the property.

rule.if: title_based_possession_suit and plaintiff_has_valid_title_under_sale and seller_did_not_deliver_possession and defendant_has_no_established_superior_title

predicates.title_based_possession_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit to recover possession on the basis of title.
predicates.plaintiff_has_valid_title_under_sale: The plaintiff established title under a sale made by a person entitled to convey the property.
predicates.seller_did_not_deliver_possession: The seller did not place the purchaser in possession when the sale was made.
predicates.defendant_has_no_established_superior_ti: The defendant did not prove a title or other right superior to the plaintiff’s title.

issues.definition: In a title-based possession suit, a purchaser with valid title may recover possession despite non-delivery by the seller when the defendant establishes no superior title.
